research_note: Curated from primary pages, abstracts and project descriptions. Books, recordings and code were not fully read, watched or executed. No verified future conference match is included in this pass. Additions checked 2026-10-17; earlier entries retain their individual source dates.

resources.title: The C to Rust Migration Book
resources.why: Covers mixed-language APIs, ownership across FFI and incremental migration exercises.
resources.caveat: Overview and contents checked; exercise solutions were not run.

resources.title: Foreign Function Interface — The Rustonomicon
resources.why: Explains calling conventions, callbacks and unsafe boundaries when Rust and C share data.

resources.title: C2Rust
resources.why: Shows automated C translation as a starting point for comparison with manual migration.
resources.caveat: The project states that translated output remains unsafe and needs further migration work.

resources.title: Rust and ThreadX
resources.why: Provides an embedded example of combining Rust with an existing C real-time operating system.
resources.caveat: Historical integration example; certification statements are tied to its publication date.

resources.title: Rust in Android: move fast and fix things
resources.why: Read a company’s account of adopting Rust alongside an existing native codebase; keep its measurements and scope explicit.
resources.caveat: 2025 company report; preserve comparison scope and measurement limits. Article sections reviewed; code and reported measurements were not reproduced.

resources.title: Comprehensive Rust
resources.why: Review ownership and other Rust foundations before studying incremental migration and language boundaries.
resources.caveat: Course introduction reviewed; exercises and full course not executed or completed.

resources.title: 100 Exercises To Learn Rust
resources.why: Use short exercises to identify gaps in Rust fundamentals before attempting migration exercises.
resources.caveat: Course introduction reviewed; exercises not executed.
